name: lucide-icon-type-is-lucideicon
hook: Use LucideIcon type from lucide-react, not ForwardRefExoticComponent
body:
When typing icon props that accept lucide-react icons, import `LucideIcon` directly:

  import { type LucideIcon } from 'lucide-react'

Do NOT use `ForwardRefExoticComponent<...>` for this purpose. `LucideIcon` is the correct named type exported by lucide-react (verified in node_modules). Confirmed by inspecting Icon.tsx in src/ui/web/shared/Icon which also uses `type LucideIcon`.

Why: The ForwardRefExoticComponent pattern is the underlying implementation detail; LucideIcon is the public-facing type alias that lucide-react exports for this purpose.

How to apply: See src/app/(frontend)/start/_components/NewStartPage/features-data.ts for the correct usage.
why: Using the correct LucideIcon type avoids verbose type definitions and is the documented approach in the project's own Icon component.

name: body-class-landing-page
hook: Document body class side effects with a comment
body:
When using document.body.classList.add('landing-page') to hide header/footer, add a comment explaining what the class does and where it is defined.

Why: 'landing-page' is a side effect that is invisible in the component tree and easy to accidentally break.

How to apply: Add a comment like '// .landing-page body class hides site header/footer (defined in globals.css)' before the useEffect.
why: Without documentation, future developers may remove this useEffect assuming it's dead code.

name: ref-for-pending-state-in-timeout
hook: Use useRef to track pending state in setTimeout callbacks
body:
When updating state inside a setTimeout and the state update could fail (e.g. due to React batch limits), use a useRef to track the pending value so it can be rolled back on error.

Why: A setTimeout closure captures stale state if the enclosing state updates. Using a ref (not state) for the pending value lets the error handler access the current pending value even after the enclosing state has changed. The error handler then rolls back by filtering the user message out of state.

How to apply: See handleSimulationSend in NewStartPage/index.tsx — pendingAiRef tracks the AI message text while the user message is in-flight.
why: Without a ref, the error handler would not know what text was pending, making it impossible to correctly roll back a partially-applied state update.
